name: Question 16
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a=⟨0,5⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(3,-3)$ and has velocity $⟨1,0⟩$ when $t=2,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨0,5⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 0\,\text{d}t,\int 5\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{C}_{1},\,5t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(2)=⟨1,\,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨{C}_{1},\,5(2)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,10+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=1$ and ${C}_{2}=-10.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨1,\,5t-10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨1,\,5t-10⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 1\,\text{d}t,\int (5t-10)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨t+{C}_{3},\,\frac{5{t}^{2}}{2}-10t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(2)=⟨3,-3⟩.$ Substituting $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨2+{C}_{3},\,\frac{5(2)^{2}}{2}-10(2)+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨3,-3⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{3},\,-10+{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{3}=1$ and ${C}_{4}=7.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨t+1,\,\frac{5{t}^{2}}{2}-10t+7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?

The acceleration a at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by a=⟨0,5⟩.

Given that the particle is at the position (3,−3) and has velocity ⟨1,0⟩ when t=2, calculate the position vector of P at time t.

a
r=⟨t2+4,5t22+7⟩
b
r=⟨t+4,5t2+72−10t⟩
c
r=⟨t+1,5t22−10t+7⟩
d
r=⟨2t+4,5t2+72−5t⟩
e
r=⟨−t2+t+1,5t22−10t+17⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector.

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨0,5⟩dt=⟨∫0dt,∫5dt⟩=⟨C1,5t+C2⟩

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(2)=⟨1,0⟩. Substituting t=2, we get

v(2)=⟨C1,5(2)+C2⟩⟨1,0⟩=⟨C1,10+C2⟩,

so we must have C1=1 and C2=−10. Therefore, the velocity vector is

v(t)=⟨1,5t−10⟩.

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

r(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫⟨1,5t−10⟩dt=⟨∫1dt,∫(5t−10)dt⟩=⟨t+C3,5t22−10t+C4⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(2)=⟨3,−3⟩. Substituting t=2, we get

r(2)=⟨2+C3,5(2)22−10(2)+C4⟩⟨3,−3⟩=⟨2+C3,−10+C4⟩,

so we must have C3=1 and C4=7. Therefore, the position of P at time t is

r(t)=⟨t+1,5t22−10t+7⟩.
